note: Gadgets section, 14-day window (336h). window_hours('2026-08-18T22:00:30Z') returns the 72h design default, so 336 is set explicitly per the gadgets/non-design rule (freshness.window_hours(now_iso, 'gadgets') == 336). Every item below was gated with `python3 pipeline/freshness.py <published_iso> 2026-08-18T22:00:30Z gadgets` and printed FRESH. Published times were read from og article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished / <time datetime> via curl, never from search snippets. Search domains theverge.com, cnet.com, wired.com, zdnet.com, arstechnica.com and reuters.com are blocked to the WebSearch user agent, so those allowed_domains were swept via their RSS feeds + direct metadata fetches instead. Notebookcheck's standard RSS path 404s; used https://www.notebookcheck.net/News.152.100.html. Collection per-source cap of 3 enforced: The Verge 3, 9to5Google 3, Android Authority 3, 9to5Mac 3, Digital Trends 2, Gizmodo 2, Notebookcheck 2, Tom's Guide 1, WIRED 1, Engadget 1, TechRadar 1 = 11 distinct outlets. Dropped as pure business/politics noise with no design hook: AI data-center/compute deals, Alibaba studio sale, Unitree IPO framing, DJI export-ban litigation, US robot import policy, Google/Spirit data purchase. Dropped as stale despite strong topical fit: Meta AI pendant reporting (Engadget 2026-05-30, TechRadar/Digital Trends/Road to VR same week), Meta Ray-Ban Display OS update (2026-03-13), Ray-Ban privacy LED update (2026-07-08), Apple wearable trifecta (Tom's Guide 2026-02-18), Copilot+ discrete-GPU test (Tom's Hardware 2026-06-14), Familiar home robot interview (TechRadar 2026-05-04), Xiaomi X20 Max robovac review (2026-08-03, 15.8d). items.title: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
items.excerpt: A promo video surfaced in a macOS beta showing Apple's camera-equipped AirPods, with the assistant narrating "See something you like? Just ask me to save it for later." It is the clearest signal yet that Apple's first always-on visual AI wearable is an audio product, not glasses — a very different interaction model for designers to plan around.

items.title: Google's Pet Memory forgot who my cats are
items.excerpt: A hands-on review of Gemini for Home's Pet Memory on Nest cameras finds the AI recognition feature confidently mislabeling pets. It is a concrete case study in what happens when an ambient AI feature ships with a confident UI but unreliable perception.

items.title: Whisker's AI-powered litter robot thinks my cats swapped bodies
items.excerpt: The $900 Litter-Robot 5 Pro uses onboard AI to identify individual pets and log their health data, but the reviewer found it repeatedly swapping identities. A pointed example of AI features being bolted onto appliance hardware faster than the recognition models can support them.

items.title: Honor finally launches Robot Phone starting at around $1,500
items.excerpt: Honor's Robot Phone ships with a motorized gimbal camera arm that physically moves and tracks subjects under AI control, starting around $1,500. It is the first mainstream phone where the AI actuates hardware rather than just processing pixels — a genuinely new form factor for shooting and framing.

items.title: Pixel 11 debuts Gboard Rambler, location-aware At a Glance, and more Gemini Intelligence
items.excerpt: The Pixel 11 launches Gemini Intelligence features including Gboard Rambler, which turns rambling speech into clean written text by stripping filler and run-on structure on device. It reframes dictation as a drafting tool rather than transcription.

items.title: Pixel Journal update brings cloud-based Private AI Compute, UI tweaks, and more
items.excerpt: Google's Journal app now routes its AI work through Private AI Compute, a cloud tier meant to carry on-device privacy guarantees off the phone. It marks the point where "on-device AI" quietly becomes a trust promise rather than a hardware constraint.

items.title: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
items.excerpt: Google shipped a Gemini for Home update adding an interactive AI Storytime mode that lets families co-create and revise stories by voice, plus wider camera support. Generative storytelling landing on a smart speaker is a real test of conversational creative tooling outside a screen.

items.title: Is the Pixel 11's Tensor G6 actually a good upgrade from the G5? I crunched the numbers
items.excerpt: A benchmark-led breakdown of Google's Tensor G6, whose TPU claims 50% more compute and 2x memory bandwidth for on-device Gemini Nano 4. Useful reality check on how much local generative headroom a 2026 flagship phone actually has.

items.title: The Airseekers Tron is an impressive mulching robot mower with a couple of frustrating flaws
items.excerpt: A long-term review of the Airseekers Tron, a vision-guided robot mower that maps and navigates a yard without boundary wire. The flaws are almost entirely interface and setup problems, not autonomy problems — a recurring pattern in consumer robotics.

items.title: Matic Cues feature lets you just talk to your robot vacuum or point at a mess to clean
items.excerpt: Matic shipped a software update adding voice and pointing-gesture control to its camera-navigated robot vacuum, so you can literally point at a spill and have it clean there. It replaces app-based room maps with deictic, in-the-room interaction — a notable shift in home robot UX.

items.title: Apple has a huge product roadmap for the smart home: Here's what's coming
items.excerpt: A rundown of Apple's incoming smart home hardware — new Apple TV, HomePod mini, and a Siri-driven smart display — all gated on the rebuilt Siri. It sketches the ambient-AI surface Apple expects designers to build for next.

items.title: 9to5Mac Overtime 077: Smart glasses are the future — Even Realities G2 CEO Will Wang
items.excerpt: Even Realities CEO Will Wang argues the case for minimal, display-light AI glasses built around restraint rather than feature maximalism. A designer-facing counterpoint to the camera-and-display arms race at Meta and Google.

items.title: Viture Pro 2 review: Affordable glasses that I loved more for work than play
items.excerpt: The Viture Pro 2 display glasses land as a cheap, comfortable virtual monitor that the reviewer preferred for productivity over media. Wearable displays as a portable workspace is a more immediate design-workflow shift than assistant glasses.

items.title: Meta's facial recognition smart glasses idea just resurfaced in a patent
items.excerpt: A newly public Meta patent describes smart glasses identifying people via AI facial recognition and expression analysis, then using that data to auto-assemble highlight media. It puts the hardest consent-design problem in wearables back on the table.

items.title: Eufy's Latest Security System Is an All-Seeing, Local-First Camera Array
items.excerpt: Eufy's Security NVR System E50 pairs up to eight PTZ cameras with a local storage box, keeping AI detection and footage off the cloud. Local-first is becoming a product positioning choice, not just an engineering one.

items.title: It's Official: No Man Can Outrun Our Robot Overlords
items.excerpt: Unitree unveiled "Superman," a humanoid clocking 12.66 m/s and two-metre standing jumps — faster than Usain Bolt's peak. The spectacle-first reveal shows how much humanoid robotics is currently designed for the demo reel.

items.title: Humanoids flop in first real firefighting drill at World Robot Games
items.excerpt: At the second World Humanoid Robot Games, 23 teams entered an outdoor firefighting and rescue event and only three survived it. The sharpest available corrective to the humanoid hype cycle, and a useful reality anchor next to the Unitree demo.

items.title: Hoverair Versa launches on Indiegogo: self-flying gimbal camera with AI auto tracking
items.excerpt: The Hoverair Versa is a 4K 60p 3-axis gimbal that clips into a flight kit to become a self-flying camera with AI subject tracking, 10-bit H-LOG and up to 17.5 stops of dynamic range. A direct workflow change for solo shooters and content designers.

items.title: I used AI to create a deli meat-inspired watch face for my Pixel Watch 5 — and now I'm questioning everything
items.excerpt: A hands-on with the Pixel Watch 5's generative watch-face tool, prompting it into an absurd deli-meat theme. Generative UI on a wearable turns watch faces from a designed asset into a prompt output, with all the taste problems that implies.

items.title: The Next Big Influencer Is This 4-Foot-Tall Robot From China
items.excerpt: The Unitree G1 has become an online star as a cheap humanoid that can charm a crowd, but WIRED asks whether it can ever hold down a real job. A study in robots designed for expressive presence rather than utility.

items.title: Things I learned about the rumored HomePod display from macOS beta code
items.excerpt: Code strings in a macOS beta reveal interface details of Apple's unannounced Siri-driven HomePod smart display. An early look at how Apple intends to give an ambient assistant a screen and a visual grammar.

items.title: G'day, Alexa+: Amazon's AI-upgraded smart home assistant has finally arrived in Australia
items.excerpt: Alexa+ launched in Australia with the LLM-powered assistant tuned to local idiom across Amazon's Echo hardware. Localisation of an agentic voice assistant is as much a voice-and-tone design problem as an engineering one.
